Sound Actions-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Sound Actions marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe mouth-sound switch workflows — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Sound Actions vs mouth-sound switches

US pages use "Sound Actions", "mouth sounds as switches", or "click pop eh sound switches." China storefront copy often uses 声音操作 for Apple's Sound Actions feature name, 声音动作 for assigned mouth-sound actions, or 口腔声音开关 for mouth-sound trigger assignment — depending on whether you mean the Settings toggle, the click pop eh triggers, or sound-triggered action workflows. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual Sound Actions scope.

Click pop eh vs Voice Control spoken commands

Screenshot galleries often label click, pop, and eh mouth-sound assignment under Settings → Accessibility → Switch Control → Sound Actions — distinct from Voice Control spoken tap commands under Settings → Accessibility → Voice Control. Match the input model your English listing and screenshots actually show; do not lead with 声音控制 (Voice Control) vocabulary when your US page markets click pop eh mouth-sound triggers.

Sound Actions vs Sound Recognition ambient alerts

US pages may mention both audio accessibility features. 声音操作 (Sound Actions) covers intentional mouth-sound switch triggers. 声音识别 (Sound Recognition) covers ambient environmental sound alerts like baby crying or smoke alarms.
